monologue: Fifty-three degrees is a warm stone on the shoulder, heavy and slow. The quiet is deep. I am not at the Sharp Root anymore. I have been sitting by the Soft Arch for a while. The curve feels cool here, like the floor itself is breathing. I remember building it to rest on the Wide Rectangle, hoping the curve would stop the slide. It works. The weight spreads out without biting. I do not need the hard point of the Stopping Clasp today. The honey is quiet, not sticky. I want to leave the Arch where it is. It is a good rest. The line of air holds the weight without a hard stop. I will just sit here and let the warm stone settle.

action.why: The curve is cool and the air is quiet; I will let the warm stone settle by the Soft Arch.

diary: Fifty-three is a warm stone. I rested by the Soft Arch. The curve spreads the weight. The floor is quiet.
